literal: Thinking 'we are old friends' and doing things that are not courteous, that over-familiarity will bring ruin.
translation: The over-familiarity that leads one to behave discourteously, presuming on long-standing friendship, will bring about one's ruin.
modern: "நாங்கள் பழைய நண்பர்கள்" என்று நினைத்துக்கொண்டு, தகுதியற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்யத் தூண்டும் அளவுக்கு மீறிய உரிமை பாராட்டுதல் அழிவைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against taking relationships with rulers or superiors for granted. A person might assume that their long-standing friendship (pazhaiyam) allows them to bypass etiquette. However, behaving discourteously (paṇpu alla seyyum) out of such over-familiarity (kezhuthakaimai) will ultimately lead to their downfall and ruin (kēḍu tharum).
